channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Is Prohibition Making Things Worse? | GFN Voices 2026 #2
item.description: Prohibition often promises fewer problems, but the aftermath tells a different story. Once safer nicotine products are pushed out of legal reach, people do not simply stop wanting them — they find other routes, often with less oversight and more risk. For smokers, that can mean returning to cigarettes or relying on unregulated supply. The real test is not whether prohibition sounds protective, but whether it leaves people safer than before. (Published on August 06, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Experts Recommend Physicians Use Vape to Help Smokers Quit
item.description: Doctors are often the first trusted voice a smoker hears when trying to quit. If evidence supports vaping as a cessation aid, clinicians should be able to discuss it honestly rather than avoid the subject because of stigma. The goal is not to promote nicotine use, but to help people move away from combustible tobacco when other methods have not worked. Smoking cessation advice should reflect the full range of evidence-based options available to adults. (Published on August 06, 2026bytobaccoreporter.com)

item.title: Relative affordability of heated tobacco products and cigarettes: a cross-country comparative analysis of 55 countries
item.description: Affordability can decide whether harm reduction is realistic or theoretical. A cross-country analysis of 55 countries found that heated tobacco products are often less affordable than cigarettes, especially in lower-income settings and among lower-income groups. That matters because price shapes behaviour: if lower-risk alternatives cost more than cigarettes, switching becomes harder for the people who may need it most. Tobacco policy should look beyond tax rates alone and consider the real consumer price of moving away from combustion. (Published on August 07, 2026byspringer.com)

item.title: Responses to FDA Tobacco Regulatory Actions
item.description: Regulatory meetings should be judged by whether they bring public health closer to real-world solutions. Responses to the FDA’s tobacco regulatory agenda show how wide the gap remains between precaution, evidence and the needs of adults who smoke. If the process treats lower-risk nicotine products mainly as a threat, it risks missing their potential role in reducing exposure to combustible tobacco. Better regulation starts with listening to evidence, consumers and unintended consequences — not only institutional caution. (Published on August 07, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Latest developments in the use of e-cigarettes by people with schizophrenia spectrum disorders who smoke: a scoping review
item.description: Smoking is a major but often neglected driver of poor health among people with schizophrenia spectrum disorders. A 2026 scoping review found preliminary evidence that e-cigarette interventions may be feasible and acceptable in this group, with signs of smoking reduction, short-term abstinence and reduced exposure to tobacco-related carcinogens. The evidence is still limited, with only a small number of studies and important questions about long-term support and generalisability. But for a population where conventional cessation often performs poorly, harm reduction deserves serious clinical attention. (Published on August 07, 2026byfrontiersin.org)
